newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GIMV, GBL, Bekaert lead Brussels bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: GIMV, GBL, Bekaert lead Brussels bourse higher.

text.p: Shares in holding companies GIMV and GBL and steel cord and wire maker Bekaert led the Brussels bourse higher in early trading on Thursday.
A stable dollar and bonds and the prospect of strong second-half earnings reports boosted sentiment, despite Wall Street's 68-point overnight fall .DJI.
By 0900 GMT, after one hour of trade, the Bel-20 index .BFX stood 7.75 points or 0.34 percent higher at 2381.64.
Flemish holding company GIMV, which made its debut on the bourse, was at 2095 francs, up on its 2010 IPO price.

Generale Bank said in its daily Belgian Equity Focus it estimated GIMV's net asset value at 2,381 francs per share, adding that it expected the market to slap a lower discount to NAV on GIMV shares than on other, more traditional holding companies.
"We would not be surprised with a discount of about 10 percent, so that the price could rise to about 2,150 francs," the bank said.
Half of GIMV's portfolio consists of its stake in electronics group Barco, the rest of minority stakes in some 200 Flemish growth companies.

"Although the GIMV must be considered mainly as a growth stock, we will have a policy of regularly increasing our dividend, depending on inflation and the GIMV's profits," board chairman Rainier van Outryve d'Ydewalle said at a ceremony in the Flemish parliament to mark the first day of trading in GIMV.
Bekaert was up 3.09 percent at 24,175 francs, continuing its recent rally. "I can see this share at 25,000 soon," one dealer said.
Cement maker CBR, down 3.46 percent at 3350 francs, was hit by a Generale Bank 'sell' recommendation.
Retailer GIB corrected from its recent rise, easing 0.29 percent to 1,730 francs.

"GIB is a stock to watch. If management does not restructure that mammoth, it will be the next target for a hostile offer from some large French, Dutch or British retail group," Alexander Pechovitch of brokerage Mignon said.
Retailer Colruyt, due to report earnings after the close of trade, was up 1.31 percent at 17,425 francs.

Dealers said expectations for Colruyt results were positive. The consensus forecast as quoted on Reuters Equities 3000 is for earnings per share to rise to 654.50 francs in the year to March 1997 and to 723 francs in the year to March 1998.
Pre-tax EPS was 518 francs in the year to March 1996.
There was also continued speculation that Colruyt may announce a sale or a bourse flotation of its Dolmen computer unit.
